quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in place by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. The Pacific Northwest is home to the Rufous hummingbird, one of the feistiest species despite being no bigger than a ping pong ball.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Deer on the Olympic Peninsula
short_read.teaser: Black-tailed deer are some of the most common residents of the Olympic Peninsula, yet they lead surprisingly complex social lives. Learn about their seasonal habits and how they've adapted to life in the temperate rainforest.

medium_read.title: How Plants Know When It's Time to Bloom
medium_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that plants can actually measure the length of day and night to time their flowering perfectly. This fascinating article explores the internal clocks that help gardens burst into color at just the right moment.

long_read.title: The Women Who Preserved America's Wildflowers
long_read.teaser: In the early 1900s, a movement of dedicated botanists and conservationists worked to save America's native wildflowers from extinction. Their legacy lives on in the beautiful meadows and forests we enjoy today, including those right here in Olympic National Park.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season
port_angeles.description: August is peak pupping season for harbor seals in the Strait of Juan de Fuca! These adorable pups are born able to swim and can often be spotted with their mothers near Ediz Hook and along the waterfront. Remember to admire them from a distance of at least 100 yards to keep both you and the seals safe.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while hovering.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're right — a hummingbird's tiny heart beats incredibly fast to power those rapid wings!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! These tiny birds have hearts that beat around 1,260 times per minute — that's more than 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These remarkable little birds have hearts that beat about 1,260 times per minute while hovering — that's incredibly fast to fuel all that energy!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: A hummingbird's metabolism is so fast that they must eat approximately every 10 minutes and consume up to half their body weight in sugar daily. At night, they enter a hibernation-like state called torpor to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderfully done! Pillangó is indeed the Hungarian word for butterfly — such a musical word for such a beautiful creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound lovely? (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungary is home to over 160 species of butterflies, including the stunning Swallowtail. Many Hungarian gardens traditionally include butterfly-friendly flowers like lavender and buddleia.

puzzle_3.question: Which tree is known as the 'Tree of Life' by indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! The Western Red Cedar was called the 'Tree of Life' because it provided so much — from canoes and longhouses to clothing and medicine. It's still deeply revered today.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The Western Red Cedar earned the name 'Tree of Life' from indigenous peoples because every part of the tree was used — for canoes, homes, clothing, baskets, and medicine. These magnificent trees can live over 1,000 years!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Western Red Cedars in the Olympic Peninsula can grow over 200 feet tall and 20 feet in diameter. Their naturally rot-resistant wood made them invaluable for building ocean-going canoes.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Western Red Cedar — Olympic National Park
